Thai Banking Sector Grapples with Major Ransomware Attack as Operations Disrupted

A significant ransomware attack targeting Thailand’s banking sector has disrupted operations at multiple financial institutions, as the industry scrambles to contain the unfolding incident. The attack, which began early Tuesday morning, has led to the temporary closure of digital banking services and affected several branches’ ability to serve customers, according to statements from the Thai Banking Federation.

The incident, described by experts as one of the most serious cyber threats to the country’s financial system in recent years, has impacted IT systems at leading industry players including Siam Capital Bank, First Thai National Bank, and Eastern Pacific Bank. Several firms reported that online banking platforms, mobile apps, and ATM networks were either partially or completely offline as of Wednesday afternoon.

Bank staff at affected sites have been instructed to follow emergency protocols, with many branches operating on a limited basis as IT teams work to isolate compromised systems and restore critical services. “At this time, our branches remain open for cash transactions, but a number of digital services remain unavailable while we address the incident,” a spokesperson for First Thai National Bank said. “We are prioritizing the safety and privacy of our customers’ data and working closely with authorities to resolve the situation.”

The Thai Banking Federation issued a joint statement confirming that several member banks had received ransom demands from the attackers, who claim to have encrypted sensitive data and threatened to leak confidential information unless payments are made. The federation emphasized that no customer deposits had been lost or stolen, but warned the situation remains fluid.

Industry analysts say the attack underscores the growing threat of cybercrime to Southeast Asia’s financial sector. “This incident highlights the urgent need for robust cybersecurity measures across the banking industry,” said Nopparat Charoensuk, a Bangkok-based financial security consultant. “The disruption to core banking services poses significant challenges for daily operations and customer trust.”

Bank workers’ unions expressed concern for employees dealing with anxious customers and heightened workloads during the disruption. “Our members are doing their utmost to maintain service and support clients, but the unprecedented nature of this attack is creating considerable stress on frontline staff,” said Kittima Thanthong, chair of the National Bank Employees Association.

As the situation develops, banks have set up dedicated hotlines and information points to keep customers informed. Authorities from the Bank of Thailand and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society are coordinating with affected firms to investigate the breach and support remediation efforts.

At press time, no timeline had been announced for the full restoration of digital banking services, and industry leaders cautioned that further disruptions are possible as recovery efforts continue.
